survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports descriptive PISA 2022 results for Cambodia using the OECD/PISA 2022 Database. The note does not specify whether student/sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the computations shown, but PISA estimates are produced under a complex sampling design and typically require the use of PISA-provided sampling weights and variance estimation procedures. The factsheet also reports uncertainty via 95% confidence intervals, implying that standard PISA variance estimation was used even though the specific weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) and replicate method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are not stated here. For users reproducing these estimates from microdata, the recommended approach is to apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the PISA 2022 database for Cambodia and the relevant domains (mathematics, reading, science).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Cambodia factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Cambodia performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to PISA 2017. Cambodia participated for the first time in PISA in 2017 under PISA for Development, and in 2022 the note reports that 5,279 students in 183 schools completed the assessment (paper-and-pencil, two-hour test) along with a background questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance comparisons to the OECD average, proficiency-level attainment (e.g., Level 2+ and Level 5/6 shares), and trends from 2017 to 2022, including changes in score gaps across socio-economic quintiles and gender differences. It also highlights that Cambodia’s data met PISA quality standards, and it uses uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) for reported estimates. No machine-learning modeling is conducted in this document; it is a descriptive reporting of PISA results and policy-relevant patterns.
